Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Holdings's Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; David Kim, Chief Strategy Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Hayes, Chief Regulatory Officer; and Jennifer Lee, Chief Communications Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational performance in our generation fleet, continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, effective cost management, progress on our infrastructure investments including the successful integration of the Desert Sun Solar Farm, advancement of our Clean Fleet 2030 program, positive regulatory outcomes in PJM, enhanced community engagement in Texas Panhandle communities, and disciplined financial execution across EPS, guidance, storm recovery, and our dividend strategy.

To give you more detail on these key areas, I'll turn it over to our CFO, Michael Chen, who will walk through the operational and financial highlights underscoring our results.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Let's start with our generation fleet performance and availability, which remains a cornerstone of our operational excellence and underpins our ability to deliver reliable, low-cost power to customers across our 12-state footprint in PJM, MISO, ERCOT, and SPP markets.

For the quarter, our equivalent availability factor—or EAF—across the entire 28 GW fleet came in at 93.2%, up 150 basis points year-over-year and exceeding our internal target of 92%. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter above 92%, reflecting the resilience of our assets amid volatile weather, including polar vortex remnants in the Midwest and sustained heat domes in Texas. On a trailing 12-month basis, fleet-wide EAF stands at 93.5%, positioning us in the top quartile of our peer group, as benchmarked against EIA's Form 860 data and NEP's composite indices.

By asset class, our thermal fleet—14 GW of combined-cycle gas turbines and simple-cycle peakers—delivered an EAF of 94.8%, a 220 basis points improvement year-over-year. Key drivers include the completion of our FleetRevive overhaul on three GE Vernova 7HA.02 units at Liberty Creek and Prairie Wind plants in MISO South. These upgrades with advanced dry low-NOx combustors and Siemens' MindSphere IoT for real-time vibration monitoring reduced forced outage rates by 35% quarter-over-quarter. Unplanned outages totaled just 1.2% of scheduled runtime, down from 2.8% last year, thanks to predictive analytics from GE's Predix suite, which preempted a rotor imbalance on our largest H-class unit.

Capacity factors for the CCGT fleet averaged 62%, bolstered by strong dispatch in PJM's BRA auction, clearing 95% of offered capacity at RPM prices averaging $115 per kW-year. In ERCOT, flex-ramp assets achieved 98.5% availability during the August heat wave, contributing 2.1 TWh and $18 million in ancillary services, up 40% year-over-year.

Our nuclear fleet—4.2 GW, anchored by the 2.4 GW dual-unit Seabrook Station in ISO-NE and 1.8 GW Prairie Island BWRs in MISO—posted a 92.7% EAF, flat year-over-year but with zero refueling outages. Capacity factor reached 93.1%, driven by Framatome's GAIA fuel software improving burnup by 4% per assembly. At Prairie Island, post-Fukushima FLEX upgrades and new hydrogen recombiners secured a 10-year PPA extension with Xcel Energy at 12% IRR. The ADVANCE Act accelerates our SMR pipeline, with NuScale's VOYGR in FERC queue for a 300 MW SPP project by 2029.

Renewables shone brighter: Our 8.5 GW portfolio—60/40 wind-to-solar—hit a 38.2% capacity factor, up 300 basis points despite low Plains winds. Wind, including our 1.2 GW Orsted-partnered Revolution Wind offshore and 2.1 GW Texas Panhandle onshore, delivered 4.8 TWh at 98.1% availability. ERCOT wind farms cut curtailment 22% to 4.5% via 450 MW/900 MWh BESS at Coyote Ridge—our first Fluence Gridstack—boosting effective capacity to 45%.

Solar at 26.4% across 3.4 GW, led by California CAISO desert assets generating 1.2 TWh despite dust. First Solar Series 7 modules with Nextracker reduced soiling 18% via AI cleaning. In PJM, renewables outperformed queue average by 12%, securing 85% RECs under RGGI. ERCOT congestion mitigated by 200 MW/400 MWh Form Energy iron-air storage pilot dispatching 150 GWh during ORDC scarcity.

Fleet-wide forced outages fell to 1.8% from 3.1%, with 25% more digital twin adoption via AspenTech yielding 3.5x ROI on $150 million YTD O&M tech. Weather-normalized output rose 7% to 28.4 TWh, beating merchant margins by 5%.

Under Clean Fleet 2030, we're targeting 50% carbon-free by 2028, with hydrogen blending up to 20% green H2 from Platte Valley electrolyzer with Plug Power, cutting Scope 1 emissions 15%. AI forecasting from AutoGrid positions us for PJM 2025/26 auctions at $140/kW-year. Supply chain risks mitigated by Vestas and LONGi offtakes covering 80%.

This 93.2% EAF and 7% output growth fueled our 12% EBITDA beat, with $450 million YTD capex on high-ROI upgrades for sustained free cash flow into 2025.

Next, on investments in renewable energy and the clean energy transition—one of our highest-conviction growth drivers. We've positioned Apex Power Holdings at the forefront, delivering 10-12% blended IRR on renewables, outpacing thermal assets.

In 2023, we deployed $2.8 billion CapEx to renewables and storage—45% of total, up from 32% in 2021—growing capacity to 8.2 GW or 42% of our 19.5 GW fleet excluding pumped hydro. Year-to-date, 1.1 GW new solar like 450 MW Desert Bloom in ERCOT and 650 MW onshore wind including 300 MW Gale Force in PJM. Adjusted FFO from renewables hit $450 million, up 28%, with 32% solar and 42% wind capacity factors via bifacial modules and Siemens Gamesa 5.X turbines.

Our five-year $18-22 billion CapEx targets 60% renewables by 2030 and net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2045, with 85% PPAs at $35-45/MWh fixed and $120 million YTD RECs.

For dispatchable clean power, 1.2 GW/4.8 GWh BESS across 12 sites, like 400 MW/1.6 GWh Ironclad in Texas with solar, at 92% efficiency using Tesla Megapacks and Fluence, capturing $200/MWh CAISO peaks. LCOE at $28/MWh, 20% below gas peakers, stacking 30% ITC.

Next-gen: 200 MW green H2 electrolyzer at Port of Long Beach with Plug Power for 20,000 tons by 2026, blending for 50% emissions cuts at $3/kg. CCUS on two 500 MW coal units with Mitsubishi capturing 90% CO2 for EOR and $50 million 45Q credits. Offshore wind talks for 500 MW Revolution Wind in ISO-NE.

Regionally: ERCOT (25% queue) avoids curtailment via GE Vernova AI; California storage boom (40% pipeline) hedges NEM 3.0; PJM/MISO capacity at $250/kW-year premiums. India JV 15% in 1 GW Rajasthan solar for 9% yields.

This hedges thermal retirements amid EV/data center growth. JVs with NextEra/Brookfield cut equity 30%. Our 12 GW queue leads Exelon's 8 GW, 60% storage attachment vs. Dominion's 45%.

Supply chains improved with 5% panel declines; queues delayed but IRA $1.2 billion tax equity and $50/ton carbon help. $3.2 billion 2024 commissioning for 15% FCF by 2026, 12-14% IRRs.

Turning to forward-looking statements and implications: These are based on current expectations, with risks in 10-K/10-Q like commodity volatility, supply chains, weather, FERC Order 1920.

We target 7-9% adjusted EPS CAGR through 2028 from this quarter's $1.42 beat: 6% organic from rate base/renewables, 1-3% productivity via 85% complete ERP for $150 million O&M synergies. FFO-to-debt 21-23% vs. 15-17% covenants.

Five-year $14-16 billion CapEx, 65% renewables/storage: 2025 $1.2 billion for 1.2 GW solar+BESS like 400 MW Desert Sun, IRA PTCs; 800 MW BESS; nuclear uprates adding 200 MW.

Portfolio to 55% renewables/zero-carbon by 2030 on 25 GW, with 200 MW H2 pilot, $300 million CCUS capturing 1.5 MtCO2.

ERCOT 5.2% load CAGR from 15 GW data centers; MISO electrification 3-4%; Northeast hedged. Demand up 25% by 2030 per EIA, gas at $3.20/MMBtu, 80% 2026 hedged $3.50.

Bolt-on M&A $1.5 billion dry powder; repurchases; $400 million grid mod with ABB DERMS. Implies 8-10% TSR, 5% dividend growth.

On O&M expense management and efficiency gains: Q3 O&M $285 million, down 8.2% or $26 million year-over-year, 4.1% below plan. TTM $1.12 billion, down 7.5% vs. EEI 4-5%. Core O&M/MWh $22.50, down 6.8%, offsetting 3.2% inflation, adding $18 million FCF.

Digital twins via GE Vernova Predix on 12 gas units reduced outages 22% to 2.1%, EAF 93.4%, preempting $12 million like HRSG leaks. Renewables SCADA/Vestas upgrades cut blade O&M 15%.

Supply chain: $9 million savings via Siemens alliance, 18-month fixed spares, RFID JIT down 11%. Southeast hurricane prep contained costs 5% below via US suppliers/45X.

Workforce: Apex Academy AR/VR for 1,200 techs cut overtime 14%, nuclear outages 28 to 24 days saving $6.8 million. Heat rate 1.4% to 7,620 BTU/kWh.

ERCOT down 11% with BESS 98.5%; MISO coal-gas flat compliance. 9% carbon intensity drop, targeting 6-8% 2024 reduction, $50 million AI/ORION.

This fuels 28.5% EBITDA margins, 10% dividend growth.

EPS performance and drivers: Q2 adjusted EPS $1.52, up 15% from $1.32, beating guidance $0.07, consensus $1.45 by 5%; GAAP $1.38.

Revenues $4.2 billion, up 8%; retail sales 6%, weather-normal load 4.5%, 250 MW data centers MISO South.

Regulated $0.85 EPS up 12% from $75 million Indiana rate case 9.75% ROE, $2.8 billion base, CWIP solar; MISO capacity $0.12.

Renewables/storage $0.42 up 25% from 350 MW COD like Desert Sun $32/MWh PPA, ERCOT battery $45/MWh scarcity.

T&D $0.18 steady, 10.2% ROE $1.5 billion base.

O&M up 3% to $850 million below 5% guide, 15% outage cut; fuel 22%; dep 7% $650 million, AFUDC $20 million offset interest; tax 21.5% PTCs.

GAAP $0.10 coal impairment for net-zero.

Midwest 18% growth, Southeast flat, ERCOT +$0.08. Q3 guide $1.60-1.70, FY $6.45-6.65.

Overview relative to guidance: Revenues $5.82 billion up 8%, beat $5.5-5.7B midpoint 3%; adj EBITDA $1.95B up 12% beat $1.8-1.9B; EPS $2.85 beat $2.50-2.70 7%, adj $2.92; net income $1.12B.

Regulated 45% EBITDA: $2.6B rev beat $2.4-2.5B, 4.2% load, $2.1B capex HVDC; EBITDA $950M beat 5%, ROE 11.2%.

Competitive gen 35%: merchant $2.1B beat $1.9-2.0B on ERCOT $85/MWh spark; gas 95% AV $450M uplift; renewables $1.1B beat 8% from 450 MW solar+BESS PPA, 250 MW offshore wind 92%.

ERCOT 25% growth data centers 1.2 GW; PJM 10%; CAISO mitigated curtailment with storage $120M ancillaries.

O&M $850M 2% below, digital twins/Siemens, NG $2.40 vs $2.80; fuel down 8%; capex $1.4B 60% renewables/CCUS.

Raise FY24: rev $23-23.5B, EBITDA $7.9-8.2B, EPS $11.20-11.60; 2025 8-10% EBITDA.

Storm response and recovery from Hurricane Epsilon, Category 3 landfall September 15th, 120 mph winds, flooding 1.2 million customers Florida/Georgia/Carolinas—25% rate base.

Activated EOC, 12,000 workers incl 4,500 EEI mutual aid from Duke/Southern/FPL. Restored 85% in 48 hours, 99.7% in 72; SAIDI 2.7 hours vs 4.2 benchmark -35%; SAIFI 1.8 vs Fiona +22% better via IBM Maximo OMS.

150 drones LiDAR/thermal cut inspections 60%, ID 85% damage first 12 hours, GE Vernova shaving 18 hours.

Florida 750k outages, 2,800 poles/450 miles conductor; Georgia 300k, undergrounding 35% limited to 12%; Carolinas microgrids 100% critical.

Costs $285M ($180M restore, $65M veg, $40M credits); 68% securitization Florida Hurricane Rider, rest 2025 rates; vs Ian $420M -32%. Insurance $120M Munich Re; OpEx $45M offset fuel.

$1.2B hardening past 18 months: 45k reclosers S&C, 1,200 miles underground, 500 AMI. Major SAIDI -28% since 2021.

Forward $2.8B resiliency: 200 MW BESS, Neara veg AI 70% preempt; PJM black-start credits; Georgia 9.5% ROE rider, IRA grants $150M. AFFO intact $4.65-4.75.

Finally, dividend policy: Board declared $0.52 quarterly, up 4%, annualized $2.08 yielding 4.2%; 48th consecutive increase.

TTM payout 68% adj EPS, 62% FCF in 60-75% target; 5.2% 10-year CAGR vs S&P Utils 4.1%.

1.8x GAAP/2.1x FFO coverage > Moody's A3; stress-tested gas drops/FERC delays.

Self-fund 85% $4.2B 2024 capex 60% renewables/grid, 9.8% ROE, 1.2 GW solar+BESS ITC, 400 MW offshore.

PJM $45/MWh +12%; ERCOT heat rates 8.5; CAISO hedges.

Dynamic overlay: 78% if 50% renewables by 2026; $500M repurchases <$50/share.

2024 65-70%, 4-6% growth 2025. 10-12% TSR.

Thank you. For Q3, we reported EPS of $1.85 and revenue of $5.2 billion. Capex was $1.1 billion, focused on renewable expansions and grid modernization. We anticipate 8-10% EPS growth in 2025.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. On operations, improved efficiency in CCGT plants from GE Vernova's Predix, 15% output increase. Outage rates down 25%.

David Kim: Thank you, Lisa. Strategically, exploring BESS opportunities. Evaluating acquisitions in ERCOT.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, David. Investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity, deploying Siemens' MindSphere against threats. Piloting advanced synchrophasors in MISO South.

Robert Hayes: Thank you, Elena. Approved rate case in PJM, allowing recovery of $200 million investments.

Jennifer Lee: Thank you, Robert. Community outreach in Texas Panhandle boosted positive sentiment 20%.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Michael, Lisa, David, Elena, Robert, and Jennifer. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for renewable investments?

Sarah Thompson: Certainly. As Michael detailed, we're deploying heavily with $18-22 billion over five years, targeting 60% renewables by 2030, with hybrids like Desert Bloom and BESS firming, securing PPAs and IRA benefits for strong IRRs.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: What is your outlook for EPS growth?

Michael Chen: Our 7-9% CAGR through 2028 embeds organic growth and productivity, with FCF supporting dividends and capex, hedged against volatility.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Chen: How are you mitigating storm risks?

Lisa Patel: Through $1.2 billion hardening, drones, BESS, and AI vegetation management, as in Epsilon response, reducing SAIDI significantly.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Grant with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Grant: What is the anticipated impact of regulatory approvals on earnings?

Robert Hayes: The PJM rate case unlocks $200 million recovery, flowing to higher ROE and supporting our EPS trajectory without disallowances.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and commitment to long-term shareholder value. We remain focused on executing priorities and positioning Apex Power Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
